title: ‘पछबरिया टोल’ कथामा सांस्कृतिक स्वरूप (Cultural form in the story 'Pachbaria Tol')
nepali: प्रस्तुतआलेखमाऋषिराज बरालको‘पछबरिया टोल’कथामासांस्कृतिकसैद्धान्तिक मान्यताकाआधारमा राजनीतिकसंस्कृतिको उद्घाटन गरिएको छ । यस अध्ययनले समाज, साहित्य र संस्कृतिकाबिचको सम्बन्धलाई स्पष्ट पार्नुका साथै समाजविकासको कुनै कालखण्डको यथार्थलाई पनि प्रस्तुत गर्ने प्रयास गरेको छ ।यसमापछबरिया टोल कथामा वर्णन गरिएको पूर्वी तराईको दक्षिण सीमावर्ती क्षेत्रमा बस्ने शोषित र उपेक्षितमधेशी समुदायमाहुने गैरलोकतान्त्रिकचुनावीगतिविधिलाई उद्घाटन गर्नुका साथै नेपाली समाजकाप्रभुत्वशालीवर्गद्वारा अधीनस्थवर्गमाथि गरिने अन्याय, अत्याचार, शोषण, उत्पीडनको अवस्थालाई चित्रण गर्नु यस लेखको उद्देश्य हो ।प्रस्तुतलेख तयार पार्नका लागिआवश्यक सामग्रीको सङ्कलन पुस्तकालयविधिको उपयोग गरी प्राथमिक र द्वितीयक स्रोतबाट गरिएको छ भने सांस्कृतिकअध्ययन पद्धतिको निर्माण गरी वर्गगत संस्कृति, राजनीतिक संस्कृति, परिवेशगत संस्कृति, प्रभुत्व र प्रतिरोधको अवस्थालाई विश्लेषणको आधार बनाइएको छ ।मूलधारको संस्कृतिले परिधीय संस्कृतिमाथि प्रभुत्व कायम राख्न अनेकौँषडयन्त्र र जालझेल गर्ने गर्दछ र परिधीय संस्कृतिले पनिप्रभुत्वशाली संस्कृतिकाविरुद्धमा बिस्तारै अवाजउठाउन थालेका छन् भन्ने नै प्रस्तुत लेखको मूलनिष्कर्ष हो ।
american_english: In this article, the political culture in Rishi Raj Baral's story 'Pachbariya Tol' has been unveiled on the basis of the theoretical tenets of cultural theory. This study attempts to clarify the relationship between society, literature and culture, as well as to present the reality of some period of social development. The aim of this article is to unveil the non-democratic electoral activities taking place in the exploited and neglected Madheshi community living in the southern border region of the eastern Terai, as described in the story 'Pachbariya Tol,' as well as to portray the condition of injustice, atrocity, exploitation and oppression meted out by the dominant class of Nepali society upon the subordinate class. To prepare this article, the necessary materials were collected from primary and secondary sources using the library method, and, by constructing a cultural-study methodology, class culture, political culture, contextual culture, and the state of dominance and resistance were made the basis of analysis. The central conclusion of this article is that mainstream culture carries out countless conspiracies and machinations to maintain its dominance over peripheral culture, and that peripheral culture has also gradually begun to raise its voice against the dominant culture.

This study endeavours to elucidate the relationship between society, literature and culture, as well as to present the reality of a particular period of social development. The aim of this piece is to lay bare the non-democratic electoral activities taking place in the exploited and neglected Madheshi community living in the southern border region of the eastern Terai, as depicted in the story 'Pachbariya Tol', whilst also depicting the state of injustice, atrocity, exploitation and oppression meted out by the dominant class of Nepali society upon the subordinate class. In preparing this article, the requisite material was collected from primary and secondary sources employing the library method, and, by constructing a cultural-studies approach, class culture, political culture, contextual culture, and the state of dominance and resistance were adopted as the basis of analysis. The central conclusion of the present article is that mainstream culture resorts to countless conspiracies and machinations in order to maintain its dominance over peripheral culture, and that peripheral culture too has gradually begun to raise its voice against the dominant culture.
australian_english: In this article, the political culture at work in Rishi Raj Baral's story 'Pachbariya Tol' has been brought into the open on the basis of the theoretical tenets of cultural theory. This study sets out to make clear the relationship between society, literature and culture, and to set down the reality of a particular period of social development as well. The aim of this piece is to lay bare the non-democratic electoral goings-on in the exploited and neglected Madheshi community living in the southern border region of the eastern Terai, as depicted in the story 'Pachbariya Tol', and to depict the state of injustice, cruelty, exploitation and oppression handed out by Nepali society's dominant class to the subordinate class. To get this article together, the necessary material was gathered from primary and secondary sources using the library method; by building a cultural-studies approach, class culture, political culture, contextual culture and the state of dominance and resistance were taken as the basis for analysis. The upshot of this article, its central conclusion, is that mainstream culture carries out all manner of conspiracies and machinations to keep its grip on peripheral culture, and that peripheral culture has slowly started to raise its voice against the dominant culture too.

The study's basically trying to spell out how society, literature and culture relate to one another, and to have a crack at showing what some particular stretch of social development actually looked like. The aim, really, is to drag out into the open the not-at-all-democratic electoral goings-on in the exploited and overlooked Madheshi community living down in the southern border country of the eastern Terai, as described in the story 'Pachbariya Tol', and to paint the injustice, cruelty, exploitation and oppression that Nepali society's dominant lot dish out to the subordinate lot. To put this article together, the needed material came from primary and secondary sources via the library method, and by knocking together a cultural-studies approach, class culture, political culture, contextual culture and the state of dominance and resistance were used as the yardsticks for the analysis. The big takeaway is that mainstream culture pulls all sorts of stunts and dodges to keep its grip on peripheral culture, and peripheral culture's slowly started finding its voice against the dominant lot too.
